STANZA I
Our God, our help in ages past
Our God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Our shelter from the stormy blast,
And our eternal home.
No line of this stanza quotes a verse closely; it is the hymn's own confession.
The psalm it sets
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 90:1–5, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1Lord, You have been our dwelling place through all generations. 2Before the mountains were born or You brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting You are God. 3You return man to dust, saying, “Return, O sons of mortals.” 4For in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes, or a watch of the night. 5You whisk them away in their sleep; they are like the new grass of the morning— PSALM 90:1–5 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 90
Before the hills in order stood, Or earth receiv'd her frame, From everlasting thou art God, To endless years the same. STANZA III
